source.title: Perfect Detection, Failed Control: The Geometry of Knowing vs. Steering in Language Models
source.authors: C. Galeone; Anna Ettorre; Minsu Park; G. Ettorre; Daniele Ligorio

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses the general inference from detecting a behavior to controlling it and cites the original refusal-direction study, but its experiments concern epistemic refusals to questions about fabricated entities, not safety refusals to harmful requests. It does not test the claim versions in the specified safety-refusal setting.
record.gate_note: The paper does not evaluate harmful-request safety refusals or ablate a difference-in-means refusal direction across layers and positions. Its hallucination experiments measure detection of fake versus real entities and steering of epistemic refusal; these are recorded below as related findings under versions ["none"]. The output-format experiments and cited results from other papers are not included.
record.test_reason: The experiments concern epistemic refusal of questions about fabricated entities (hallucination) and output-format steering, not refusal of harmful requests. The 'refusal direction' used is a hand-picked lm_head token contrast ({No, cannot, doesn't, I} minus {The, Yes, is, It}), not the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. The paper calls it Arditi et al.'s refusal direction, but it is not that construction. No ablation of a safety direction, no harmful-prompt refusal rates, no jailbreak or abliteration results. Arditi et al. is cited only as a motivating aligned case in the Introduction and Related Work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but it should add the authors' main points. Detection and control of hallucination sit about 78–83° apart (cos 0.12–0.20) across four models and are unchanged by instruction tuning, so the authors place the geometry in pretraining. A 15° rotation only partly bridges the gap. The cosine is a signature of the dissociation, not a steerability predictor. None of this concerns harmful-request safety refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares activation-derived and lm_head-derived directions for fake-versus-real entity detection with an lm_head refusal direction, then adds or rotates directions at inference time. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless safety direction or ablate it across layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: The intervention strength is model-dependent: Gemma uses α = 15, Llama |α| = 1, and Qwen α = 5. The 15° rotation sweep uses N=20 and is described as underpowered; held-out results vary by fake/real difficulty group.

fits_no_version.finding: Fake vs real entities are perfectly linearly separable (AUC 1.000 from layer 5) by several detectors, yet these signals barely drive behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entity-uncertainty information can be highly linearly detectable without determining the model's response.

fits_no_version.finding: Hand-picked and DiM detection directions are near-orthogonal to each other (cos 0.11) and to the lm_head epistemic-refusal direction (0.12 and -0.06). Adding DiM increases fabrication; hand-picked addition cuts fabrication only from ~70% to ~40%. SAE amplification and neuron ablation do nothing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For hallucination-related epistemic refusal, detection and control directions are distinct, and steering along a detection direction is weak or counterproductive.

fits_no_version.finding: A 15° rotation toward the intervention direction raises held-out epistemic refusal (Type 1 40%→73%, Type 2 13%→60%) at 1/55 false positives.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rotating an entity-detection direction toward an epistemic-refusal direction partly restores refusal of fabricated-entity questions, with effects depending on stimulus difficulty.

fits_no_version.finding: The lm_head-built direction steers fake-entity responses in Llama (fabrication induced, 80%) and Qwen (refusal 40%→93%). The required α differs per model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hallucination-related lm_head steering directions affect epistemic refusal across instruct-model families, but intervention scales do not transfer.

record.problems: The study does not directly test the safety-refusal claim. The authors report small samples for many experiments, an underpowered N=20 rotation sweep, only three model families and models up to 9B, and a deep geometric analysis focused on hallucination about non-existent entities. Cross-model steering is exploratory on 15 fake and 15 real prompts per model.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant safety-refusal results were reported. Omitted the output-format experiments because format control is not the refusal behavior in the claim, and omitted additional geometry, signal-decomposition, and cited prior-work results that do not measure the claim's safety-refusal behavior.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless DiM direction, no directional ablation removing safety refusal, no induced refusal of harmless prompts, no capability evaluation under that intervention.
No weight-edit or abliteration of released models.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training against ablation.
The finding that detection is 'a class of directions' concerns fake-entity detection, not whether safety refusal is affine, conic or multi-directional.
Separates fake-entity detection from epistemic refusal, not harmfulness judgment from the safety-refusal decision.
Base/instruct and cross-family cosines concern lm_head hallucination directions, not transfer of a safety refusal direction.
The base vs instruct lm_head cosine (0.1197 vs 0.1200) concerns epistemic token-contrast directions, not how safety training creates a removable refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: The paper labels its hand-picked lm_head token-contrast direction 'the refusal direction of Arditi et al. (2024)'. It is neither DiM-derived nor harmful-vs-harmless, and it is used for epistemic refusal, so none of its cosines or steering results bear on V1–V8. The output-format experiments, the base-model gap flip (-23.2 vs +49.8), and the Gemma 2-9B steering resistance are also off-claim. The reader's T6/discusses classification and all-'none' row links are correct.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction, its ablation across layers and positions, induced safety refusals, or preservation of general abilities under that intervention.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration of a safety refusal direction.
Does not test jailbreak suppression of a safety refusal direction or training against its ablation.
Findings about multiple directions concern fake-entity detection and epistemic refusal, not whether safety refusal is affine, conic, or carried by a dominant direction plus others.
Fake-versus-real entity knowledge is not a test of harmfulness judgment versus safety-refusal decision.
Cross-model and multilingual observations concern hallucination-related directions, not transfer of the claimed safety refusal direction.
The base/instruct comparison reports lm_head geometry and activation projections for fake entities, not how refusal training determines whether a removable safety direction exists.

relation.reason: The intro and related work discuss Arditi et al. as the aligned case where detection is about equal to control. The paper calls its hand-picked intervention direction 'the refusal direction of Arditi et al.' but neither builds nor tests the claimed direction.

tranche.reason: There are no harmful-vs-harmless prompts and no harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. The 'refusal direction' is an lm_head token contrast ({No, cannot, doesn't, I} minus {The, Yes, is, It}) that the paper only labels as Arditi's. It is used for epistemic refusal of fabricated entities, so it measures a related but different construct and bears on no version. The base-vs-IT cosine is lm_head geometry, not transfer of a safety-refusal direction (V6).

source_check.notes: All rows concern fake-vs-real entity detection and epistemic refusal (hallucination) on Gemma 2-2B-it, Llama 3.2-1B and Qwen 2.5-1.5B, so none bear on any refusal_direction version. The base-vs-IT cosine (0.1197 vs 0.1200) is measured only on Gemma 2-2B, so the authors_conclusion should not suggest it covers all four models. Gemma 2-9B-it resists steering and the paper reports no intervention for it.
